question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(2x+3)^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((2x+3)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3))+(x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{2x+3}\cdot 2) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)+\frac{2x}{2x+3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)+\frac{2x}{2x+3})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(2x+3)^{x}:$    

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(2x+3)^{x}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)+\frac{2x}{2x+3}) \\  & =(2x+3)^{x}\cdot (\frac{(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)}{2x+3}+\frac{2x}{2x+3}) \\  & =(2x+3)^{x-1}\cdot ((2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x+3)+2x).\end{aligned}
$$
